Subject: Post-demo econ + private deployment options (license / support / env count)

Hi Lucas / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we stay aligned. TL;DR: you’re exploring a Private (VPC/on‑prem) deployment for production-sensitive inference, target committed volumes ~750M tokens/month with occasional spikes to ~1B/month, and you’d like pricing options that map to a per‑instance license + support tier (annual) or a commit‑band model with effective $/1M token targets.

Recap (what I heard)
- Workload: two primary APIs (realtime chat + batch embeddings). Expected steady state ~750M tokens/month; peak ~1B tokens/month.
- Envs: 3 logical environments (prod, staging, internal-test) with an ask for a 4th short‑lived sandbox for partner trials.
- SLA: 99.9% desired for prod; must be able to failover across AZs within region.
- Compliance: SOC2 in scope; you’ll need audit logs and KMS integration.

Pricing options we can assemble (we covered on call):
1) License + support (annual): fixed platform license (per cluster / per region) + 24/7 support tier (P1 on‑call) + unlimited inference at a negotiated rate. Example structure: $X/year license + $Y/year support. Effective $/1M tokens depends on commit volume — we can show math for 750M vs 1B.
2) Commit band (preferred by many customers): monthly/annual token commit with step pricing (e.g., $A per 1M tokens up to band1, $B per 1M beyond). Bands give predictable unit economics and straightforward overage billing.
3) Hybrid: modest license to cover private control plane + token commit for inference. Helpful when you need stronger isolation but still want linear unit costing.

Action items (agreed)
- Kimberly (me): send a concise cost worksheet with three scenarios (license+support, commit bands, hybrid) and two sizing models (steady 750M and peak 1B). I’ll include per-environment line items so you can see incremental cost to add the sandbox. Attachment: usage-estimate.xlsx (coming).
- SeekAI: confirm the final list of environments (prod/staging/internal-test/sandbox) and whether sandbox must be long-lived. Also confirm expected percent of tokens from chat vs batch (rough split helps sizing).
- Marissa / Rishi: I copied you to review the SOW draft (high level) and to add any notes on dedicated capacity constraints or discounts for multi-year commits.

Next meeting: propose Wed 2027-04-21 10am PDT to walk the worksheet and redlines. Let me know if that works.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
